title: performance canary: adaptive KV-aware hysteresis and auto-detection rollout guards
author: Aisha Khan
summary: Introduce adaptive, KV-cache-aware hysteresis and enhanced auto-detection logic for the performance canary service to reduce false positives during transient load and KV warmup.
description: Motivation: our existing perf canary flagged transient regressions during KV-cache warmups and short traffic spikes which caused unnecessary rollbacks and manual interventions. This PR enhances the canary detector with an adaptive hysteresis layer that factors in KV cache hit-rate and ongoing traffic variance, plus an auto-detection mode that tunes thresholds per-model/shape. Changes: 1) new KV-aware hysteresis algorithm in perf_canary.detector that delays decision boundaries when cache_warmup is detected and increases sensitivity decay based on observed hit-rate trends; 2) auto-detection component that collects short rolling histograms of latency and throughput per model/route and suggests per-route thresholds stored in the canary config; 3) rollout guard integration that prevents automated canary flips when KV warmup or transient autoscaling events are detected; 4) metrics and tracing hooks added to observability so incidents can be diagnosed (canary.decisions, canary.kv_warmup_score, canary.threshold_suggestion); 5) docs and upgrade notes. Backwards compatibility: detector defaults preserve current behavior unless adaptive_kv_hysteresis is enabled in the canary policy. Testing: unit tests for hysteresis math, integration test that simulates KV warmup and verifies guard prevents premature rollback, and end-to-end simulation against perf-canary lab harness. Risk: low to medium; algorithm adds stateful behavior in detector. Rollout: gated behind feature flag and can be toggled per-tenant. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.
